title.en: Going to sleep, going to buy
title.de: Ich gehe schlafen, ich gehe kaufen
title.it: Vado a dormire, vado a comprare

goal.en: You can say who is off to do what: Grem spat. Pridi jest! Luka gre past ovce. And after moram, hočem the full infinitive.
goal.de: Du sagst, wer losgeht, um etwas zu tun: Grem spat. Pridi jest! Luka gre past ovce. Und nach moram, hočem den ganzen Infinitiv.
goal.it: Sai dire chi va a fare che cosa: Grem spat. Pridi jest! Luka gre past ovce. E dopo moram, hočem l'infinito intero.

say.en: After a verb of going, what you go to do isn't the infinitive but the supine (*namenilnik*): the infinitive without its last **-i**. spati → **spat**: **Grem spat.** (I'm off to sleep.) delati → **delat**: **Tone gre delat.** (Tone is going to work.)
say.de: Nach einem Verb des Gehens steht, was man tun geht, nicht im Infinitiv, sondern im Supinum (*namenilnik*): der Infinitiv ohne sein letztes **-i**. spati → **spat**: **Grem spat.** (Ich gehe schlafen.) delati → **delat**: **Tone gre delat.** (Tone geht arbeiten.)
say.it: Dopo un verbo di movimento, quello che si va a fare non è l'infinito ma il supino (*namenilnik*): l'infinito senza l'ultima **-i**. spati → **spat**: **Grem spat.** (Vado a dormire.) delati → **delat**: **Tone gre delat.** (Tone va a lavorare.)

examples.en: I'm tired, I'm off to sleep.
examples.de: Ich bin müde, ich gehe schlafen.

examples.sl: Tone gre zjutraj delat v kovačnico.
examples.en: In the morning Tone goes to work in the smithy.
examples.de: Morgens geht Tone in der Schmiede arbeiten.
examples.it: La mattina Tone va a lavorare nella fucina.

ask.explain:
**gredo** (going) → the supine: spati → **spat**
- Otroci gredo spat. · The children are off to sleep.

say.en: The verbs of going are **iti** (go), **priti** (come), **oditi** (leave), **hoditi** (go regularly), and **poslati** or **peljati** someone: **Pridi jest!** (Come and eat!) **Luka pelje ovce pit.** (Luka takes the sheep to drink.) **Vida pošlje Nejca kupit kruh.**
say.de: Die Verben des Gehens sind **iti** (gehen), **priti** (kommen), **oditi** (weggehen), **hoditi** (regelmäßig gehen), und jemanden **poslati** (schicken) oder **peljati** (bringen): **Pridi jest!** (Komm essen!) **Luka pelje ovce pit.** (Luka bringt die Schafe zum Trinken.) **Vida pošlje Nejca kupit kruh.**
say.it: I verbi di movimento sono **iti** (andare), **priti** (venire), **oditi** (andarsene), **hoditi** (andare di solito), e **poslati** (mandare) o **peljati** (portare) qualcuno: **Pridi jest!** (Vieni a mangiare!) **Luka pelje ovce pit.** (Luka porta le pecore a bere.) **Vida pošlje Nejca kupit kruh.**

examples.sl: Luka pelje ovce pit k potoku.
examples.en: Luka takes the sheep to the stream to drink.
examples.de: Luka bringt die Schafe zum Bach zum Trinken.
examples.it: Luka porta le pecore a bere al ruscello.

ask.explain:
**pridi** (come) → the supine: jesti → **jest**
- jesti · the infinitive, after moram, hočem

say.en: The supine never changes: the verb of going says who and when. **Greva spat.** (We two are off to sleep.) **Luka je šel iskat Belo.** (Luka went to look for Bela.) **Jutri bom {m:šel|f:šla} kupit kruh.** What it does to comes after it, as after any verb: **kupit kruh**, **iskat Belo**.
say.de: Das Supinum ändert sich nie: das Verb des Gehens sagt, wer und wann. **Greva spat.** (Wir zwei gehen schlafen.) **Luka je šel iskat Belo.** (Luka ist Bela suchen gegangen.) **Jutri bom {m:šel|f:šla} kupit kruh.** Was es betrifft, folgt danach wie nach jedem Verb: **kupit kruh**, **iskat Belo**.
say.it: Il supino non cambia mai: il verbo di movimento dice chi e quando. **Greva spat.** (Noi due andiamo a dormire.) **Luka je šel iskat Belo.** (Luka è andato a cercare Bela.) **Jutri bom {m:šel|f:šla} kupit kruh.** L'oggetto viene dopo, come dopo ogni verbo: **kupit kruh**, **iskat Belo**.

examples.en: Luka went to look for Bela.
examples.it: Luka è andato a cercare Bela.

examples.en: Tomorrow we're going to buy a new hammer.
examples.de: Morgen gehen wir einen neuen Hammer kaufen.
examples.it: Domani andiamo a comprare un martello nuovo.

ask.text: Včeraj sta Nejc in Tine šla ___ žabe. (loviti)
ask.hint: šla: going; the supine never changes
ask.explain:
**sta šla** says who and when; the supine stays: loviti → **lovit**
- sta šla lovit žabe · they went to catch frogs

say.en: A verb with **se** keeps its **se**, and **se** goes to second place as always: **Gremo se kopat.** (Let's go for a swim.) **Otroci se gredo igrat.** (The children are going to play.)
say.de: Ein Verb mit **se** behält sein **se**, und **se** steht wie immer an zweiter Stelle: **Gremo se kopat.** (Gehen wir schwimmen.) **Otroci se gredo igrat.** (Die Kinder gehen spielen.)
say.it: Un verbo con **se** tiene il suo **se**, e **se** va al secondo posto come sempre: **Gremo se kopat.** (Andiamo a fare il bagno.) **Otroci se gredo igrat.** (I bambini vanno a giocare.)

examples.en: It's hot. Let's go for a swim!
examples.de: Es ist heiß. Gehen wir schwimmen!
examples.it: Fa caldo. Andiamo a fare il bagno!

examples.sl: Otroci se gredo igrat pod lipo.
examples.en: The children are going to play under the linden.
examples.de: Die Kinder gehen unter der Linde spielen.
examples.it: I bambini vanno a giocare sotto il tiglio.

ask.instruction: Kateri stavek je prav? · Which sentence is right?
ask.prompt: The children are going to play.
ask.explain: **se** → second place, right after otroci: Otroci **se** gredo igrat.

say.en: Only after going. After other verbs it is the full infinitive: **moram spati**, **hočem jesti**, **začnem delati**. In speech you'll hear the short form there too (*moram delat*), and that's fine; written, and in careful speech, it is **moram delati**. And **Grem spat** is going to sleep, **Grem v posteljo** going to bed: a place.
say.de: Nur nach dem Gehen. Nach anderen Verben steht der ganze Infinitiv: **moram spati**, **hočem jesti**, **začnem delati**. Gesprochen hörst du auch dort die kurze Form (*moram delat*), und das ist in Ordnung; geschrieben und sorgfältig gesprochen heißt es **moram delati**. Und **Grem spat** ist schlafen gehen, **Grem v posteljo** ins Bett gehen: ein Ort.
say.it: Solo dopo il movimento. Dopo gli altri verbi c'è l'infinito intero: **moram spati**, **hočem jesti**, **začnem delati**. Nel parlato senti anche lì la forma corta (*moram delat*), e va bene; per iscritto e nel parlato curato è **moram delati**. E **Grem spat** è andare a dormire, **Grem v posteljo** andare a letto: un luogo.

examples.en: Tomorrow I have to get up early.
Tine wants to sleep at his grandpa's.
examples.de: Tine will bei seinem Opa schlafen.

ask.explain:
**moram** isn't going → the infinitive: **delati**
- in speech also moram delat
- Grem delat. · after going: the supine

exercises.explain:
**the supine** → the infinitive without its last -i
- spati → spat · jesti → jest · brati → brat
- peči → peč · kopati se → kopat se
**gre** → the supine: pasti → **past**: Luka gre past ovce.

exercises.instruction: Dopolni z namenilnikom ali nedoločnikom · Fill in the supine or the infinitive
exercises.title: Zjutraj v vasi
exercises.text: Zjutraj vsi nekam gredo. Zala gre z Luko na pašnik ___ ovce. (pasti) Babica Micka gre v gozd ___ gobe. (nabirati) Tone gre v kovačnico ___. (delati) Vida pošlje Nejca k Antonu ___ med. (kupiti) Nejc pa teče k ribniku ___ žabe. (loviti) Stari Janez je utrujen in gre ___. (spati) Jutri bo moral spet zgodaj ___. (vstati)

gaps.explain: After **moral** (must) the infinitive: **vstati** (in speech also vstat).

exercises.translation: In the morning everyone is off somewhere. Zala goes with Luka to the pasture to graze the sheep. Granny Micka goes into the forest to pick mushrooms. Tone goes to the smithy to work. Vida sends Nejc to Anton's to buy honey. But Nejc runs to the pond to catch frogs. Old Janez is tired and goes off to sleep. Tomorrow he'll have to get up early again.

exercises.instruction: Namesto hoče povej gre · Say goes instead of wants
exercises.explain:
**hoče** + the infinitive → **gre** + the supine
- Luka hoče spati. → Luka gre spat.
- Nejc se hoče igrati. → Nejc se gre igrat.
